candidates.label: Omit FormOccurrence and carry canonical source paths on diagnostics
evidence: The refined candidate makes FormOccurrence optional and explicitly permits source_path to remain embedded in compiler diagnostics.
No serialized fixture or implementation currently demonstrates a query or diagnostic that requires an independently addressable occurrence node.
The precedent and non-vacuity reviews reject ornamental identities and require a finite need before adding a new concept.

candidates.label: Add an immutable compile-only FormOccurrence identity
evidence: The refined candidate permits FormOccurrence when one authored form is reused at multiple nested source paths and diagnostics need addressable occurrences.
Its closed shape is authored_form_ref plus canonical source_path, with no runtime state, operands, lifecycle, authority, or Work identity.
Materialization can simplify cross-reference queries when multiple defects and compilation results refer to the same reused occurrence.

candidates.label: Promote FormOccurrence into a runtime form instance
rejectionReasons: A runtime form instance duplicates or collapses WorkNode, WorkRun, Attempt, repeat-round, and journal identities.
No runtime or authority owner gate permits a source diagnostic identity to acquire execution state or lifecycle.

candidates.label: Use WorkNode identity as the authored form occurrence
rejectionReasons: One authored form occurrence may compile into multiple WorkNodes, while explicit source paths and graph-node paths occupy different identity domains.
Aliasing source occurrence with output graph identity makes rejection diagnostics impossible when no WorkGraph exists.

candidates.label: Defer the FormOccurrence decision
evidence: Deferral preserves the optional candidate but prevents the exact compiler-result and ontology schemas from closing.

candidates.label: Stop the composition-form Decision Gate
evidence: Stopping preserves current source and candidate bytes and authorizes no downstream mutation.
